{{nihongo|'''Ōyosami Shrine'''|大依羅神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

== Enshrined God ==
The deities enshrined are as follows (the place names in parentheses are the old places before they were enshrined). </ref><ref name="Anonymous-20240629112444">[https://yosami-jinja.com/page-5741/ Oyora Shrine History]</ref>.
* Main enshrined deity
** Taketoyo Hazurawake no Kimi - 9th {{ill|Emperor Kaika|ar|الإمبراطور كايكا|arz|الامبراطور كايكا|azb|کایکا (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Kaika|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کایکا|cs|Kaika|de|Kaika|es|Kaika Tennō|fa|امپراتور کایکا|fi|Kaika|fr|Kaika|hr|Kaika|id|Kaisar Kaika|it|Kaika|ja|開化天皇|ka|კაიკა|ko|가이카 천황|nl|Kaika|pl|Kaika|pt|Kaika|ru|Император Кайка|sh|Car Kaika|simple|Emperor Kaika|sl|Cesar Kajka|sr|Каика|sv|Kaika (kejsare)|th|จักรพรรดิไคกะ|tl|Emperador Kaika|tr|Kaika (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кайка|uz|Imperator Kaika|vi|Thiên hoàng Kaika|zh|開化天皇|zh_min_nan|Kaika Thian-hông|zh_yue|開化天皇|qid=Q333548}}{{ill|Imperial Prince|ja|皇子|ko|황자|vi|Hoàng tử|zh|皇子|zh_min_nan|Hông-chú|qid=Q12886381}}.
** {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013|lt=Sotsutsu no Onomikoto}} - One of the pillars of {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013}}.
** {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013|lt=Nakatsutsuno no Mikoto}} (Nakatsutsu no Mikoto) - One of the pillars of the Sumiyoshi Sanjin.
** {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013|lt=Uwatsutsu no Omikoto}} (Uwatsutsu no Onomikoto) - One of the three Sumiyoshi Gods<ref>On the homepage of Oyora Shrine, it is listed as Omotzutsu no Omikoto. </ref>.

* Deity enshrined
** {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Takamiko Omi}}, {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi no Mikoto}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Emperor Suinin}}, {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|Q10881556|qid=Q10881556|lt=Goju Takekami}}, (Kushimeigyoku no Mikoto<ref>It is listed as a deity enshrined on the home page of Oyora Shrine.</ref>)

* Enshrined deity** Kusatsu Otoshi Okami (Shikiuchi Shrine, Karita), Nunotahime Okami (Shikiuchi Shrine, Sugimoto), {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Kenhaya Susano Okami}} (Abiko), {{ill|Kushinadahime|Q505469|qid=Q505469|lt=Kinada Hime Daijin God}} (Sugimoto), Yabashira Miko Okami (Sugimoto), {{ill|Oyamakui no Kami|Q10935105|qid=Q10935105|lt=Oyama Kui Okami}} (Niwai), {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susaki no Mikoto}} (Sugimoto), Susaki no Mikoto (Yamanouchi)

In "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}, which was established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), there are four enshrined deities. There are also four dais in the Aino-sai-jo under the Shiji-sai of the Engishiki, the Aino-sai-jo of the special festival, the {{ill|Yasojima Festival|Q24870749|qid=Q24870749|lt=Yasojima-shin-sai}} article, the Koriame-jin-sai-jo, and the Meishin-sai-jo. Kusatsu Otoshi Okami and the following were enshrined together in {{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}40).

== About the enshrined deity ==
[[File:Oyosami-jinja, Yosamiike-ato.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Oyosami Pond Monument}}]]The name ``Ira'' of Oyora Shrine and its divine name refers to the place name {{Sfn|Oyora Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. In "{{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542|lt=Japanese Namesho}}", {{ill|Settsu Province|Q864163|qid=Q864163}}{{ill|Sumiyoshi district|ja|住吉郡|zh|住吉郡|qid=Q10885872}} is located in Oyosamigo (near Oyora Shrine) and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawachi Province}} Irago (currently the northwestern part of {{ill|Matsubara|Q774952|qid=Q774952}}) can be seen in {{ill|Tajihinokōri district|Q11368538|qid=Q11368538}}, and it is said that the name of the place covered that area {{Sfn|Oyora Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. It is assumed that ``Oyira Shrine'' was originally enshrined as a local deity in Yorami (Yira) {{Sfn|Oyira Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. Regarding this Yomi area, there is an old article in the ``{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}'' {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}} period<ref group="hara">``Nihon Shoki'' written in October 62 of Emperor Sujin. </ref>・{{ill|Empress Suiko|Q298057|qid=Q298057}} period <ref group="Hara"> "Nihon Shoki" Emperor Suiko's 15th year (607) Koresaijo. </ref> shows that "{{ill|Yorami Pond|Q65248853|qid=Q65248853}}" is built {{Sfn|Oyora Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. This Iami Pond was a large-scale reservoir built by the royal power to cultivate farmland, but it was built in the first year of {{ill|Hōei|Q1145262|qid=Q1145262}} ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=1704}}), most of them disappeared due to the {{ill|replacement work|Q131618748|qid=Q131618748|lt=replacement work}} of {{ill|Yamato River|arz|نهر ياماتو|ceb|Yamato Gawa|es|Río Yamato|fa|رود یاماتو|fr|Yamato-gawa|gl|Río Yamato|it|Yamato (fiume)|ja|大和川|ko|야마토강|ru|Ямато (река)|zh|大和川|qid=Q9001527}}. However, part of it remained next to our company and came to be called Ajiemon Pond. After that, it was called Nii-no-Ike, but in {{ill|1969|Q2485|qid=Q2485}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ka|შოვას პერიოდი|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}}44) it was located next to {{ill|Q11 441189|qid=Q11 441189|lt=Hannan High School}} It was reclaimed and disappeared as a ground <ref>[https://www.city.matsubara.lg.jp/docs/page4613.html Matsubara City History Walk 36 Construction of Imo Pond]</ref>.In addition, "Nihon Shoki" {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119}} period<ref group="original">"Nihon Shoki" September 43rd year of Emperor Nintoku, Koushi Sakujo. </ref>・{{ill|Empress Kōgyoku|Q235296|qid=Q235296|lt=Emperor Kogyoku}}<ref group="Original">Nihonshoki, May 5th, 642, the first year of Emperor Kogyoku. </ref> has a description of ``Yorami Tonkura'', and ``Wamyosho'' has a description of Miyake-go (present-day northern Matsubara City) in Tanbi District, Kawachi Province, and the area was expanded with the construction of Yorami Pond. link|Tunkura|Q11465761}} (ancient territory directly under the royal authority) was also established {{Sfn|Oyora Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. The Oyira deity enshrined there was also regarded as important by the imperial court, and as mentioned later, literature records that it received offerings from the imperial court many times.In addition, in the Yoreami area, it is known that the ancient clan '''{{ill|Yosami no Otarumi|Q24899491|qid=Q24899491|lt=Yora clan}}''' (Yosamiuji, Yoreami clan/Yorami Abiko) resided {{Sfn|Oyora Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. It appears that the Yira clan was involved in the management of Yorami Tunkura, and it is also speculated that he was a member of the Hosai clan of Oyora Shrine {{Sfn|Oyora Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. The current personal deity of Oyira-jin, Kenpōha Murawawakiō, appears in ``{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}'' as the ``progenitor of Yorimino Abi Kotono,'' and is a person who is positioned as the founder of the Ira clan.{{Sfn|Oyira Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. However, in ``{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}'', Yira Sukune (Kobetsu of Settsu Province) is not listed as a descendant of Hikozamikoto}} (Prince of Emperor Kaika), rather than Kentoyo Hazurawaki, and there are discrepancies between documents {{Sfn|Ira clan (ancient clan)|2010}}. In addition, the same record also includes the Kamibetsu Yira Ren (Sakyo Jinbetsu and Ukyo Jinbetsu), Mononobe Yira Ren (Kawachi Kuni Jinbetsu), and Sone Shiya of {{ill|Paekche|Q28428|qid=Q28428|lt=Baekje Country}}. There are mentions of the descendants of Mamino-kun, such as Yiraren (from Kawachi Province), and it is said that there were multiple lines of clans that called themselves ``Yira'' {{Sfn|Ira clan (ancient clan)|2010}}. However, our company believes that the origin of the shrine is that the Yoragohiko clan enshrined their ancestor, King Kentohoha Murawaki, the fourth son of Emperor Kaika<ref name="Anonymous-20240629112444"/>.Regarding the three Sumiyoshi deities (Sokotsutsuo no Mikoto, Nakazutsuo no Mikoto, and Uetsutsuo no Mikoto) other than King Kentohohazurawaki, there is an article dated September 10, 9th year of the reign of Empress Jingu and Empress Chuai in the Pre-Sessho Period of the Nihon Shoki {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}. In </ref>, when Empress Jingu conquered {{ill|Silla|ar|مملكة شلا|ast|Silla (Corea)|az|Şila krallığı|azb|شیلا|bar|Silla|be|Сіла (дзяржава)|bg|Сила (държава)|bs|Kraljevstvo Sila|ca|Silla (Corea)|cdo|Sĭng-lò̤|ckb|شیللا|cs|Silla|da|Silla (koreansk stat)|de|Silla|eo|Silla|es|Silla (Corea)|eu|Silla (Korea)|fa|پادشاهی شیلا|fi|Silla|fr|Silla (Corée)|gl|Reino de Silla|hi|सिल्ला|hr|Kraljevstvo Sila|hu|Silla (ókori királyság)|id|Silla|it|Silla (Corea)|ja|新羅|ka|სილა|kk|Силла|km|ស៊ីលឡា|ko|신라|ks|سِللا سَلطَنَت|ku|Keyaniya Sillayê|lt|Šila (Korėja)|lv|Silla|mk|Сила (држава)|ml|സില്ല|mn|Шилла|ms|Silla|my|ရှီလာ|mzn|سیلا|nds|Silla|nl|Silla (Korea)|no|Silla|oc|Silla (reialme)|pl|Silla|pt|Silla (Coreia)|ro|Silla|ru|Силла|sco|Silla|sh|Sila (kraljevina)|si|සිල්ලා|simple|Silla|sk|Silla|sr|Сила (краљевство)|sv|Silla|sw|Silla|th|ชิลลา|tl|Silla|tr|Silla|uk|Сілла|vi|Tân La|wuu|新罗|zh|新罗|zh_classical|新羅|zh_min_nan|Sin-lô|zh_yue|新羅|qid=Q28456}}, she prayed to the three Sumiyoshi gods for victory and a safe voyage. At that time, there is a tradition that says that {{ill|Yosami no Otarumi|Q24899491|qid=Q24899491}} was appointed as the priest who enshrines the three Tsutsuo gods<ref name="Anonymous-20240629112444"/>, and this is related to {{Sfn|Oyora Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. Furthermore, according to {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}'s ``{{ill|Settsu Meisho Zue|Q11498549|qid=Q11498549}},'' there used to be four deities to be enshrined: Ōmi Takamikoto, Tsukuyomi no Mikoto, Emperor Suinin, and Igoshigu (Igoshigu) (1977}}. Even after the four main deities enshrined today were established, the previous four continue to be enshrined in the main shrine <ref name="Explanation board"/>.

== History ==

== Founding ==
Founding date is unknown. As mentioned above, it was originally enshrined as a local deity in Yoriami, and it is presumed that it was enshrined by the Yira clan in ancient times {{Sfn|Oyira Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.

Furthermore, as mentioned above, the existence of the Yorami tonkura is recognized in the Yorami area, and there is a theory that Oyira Shrine functioned as a guardian deity when this tonkura was managed by the royal power {{Sfn|Oyira Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.

=== Medieval/Early modern ===
In the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}, the social power declined with the decline of the Yoriami clan, and the company affairs came to be handled by the {{ill|Daishō kannon-ji Temple|Q11438537|qid=Q11438537}} (Fudo-in, Abiko Kannon) betto of {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}} {{Sfn|Oyora Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.

In {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}'s ``{{ill|Wakan Sansai Zue|Q1135803|qid=Q1135803}}'', ``Ino Daimyojin'' is located in ``Abiko Village,'' its special place is Daisho Kannon-ji Temple, and the enshrined deity is unknown.{{Sfn|Oyora Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. According to the description in "Sumiyoshi Matsuba Daiki," the shrine was in serious decline at the time, and it is presumed that it was only able to survive with the support of Sumiyoshi Shrine. Also, in {{ill|Manji (era)|Q1145295|qid=Q1145295}} 2nd year ({{ill|1659|Q6995|qid=Q6995}}), the main shrine, the shrine, and the hall of worship were destroyed by fire, so they were rebuilt {{Sfn|Oyora Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}<ref name="Anonymous-20240629112444"/>.

=== Modern times and later ===
In the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} period, it was separated from Daisho Kannon-ji Temple due to {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}. In the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was initially listed as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mukakusha}}, but in February {{ill|1876|Q7766|qid=Q7766}} (Meiji 9), |Q134917316}}, and in January 1907|Q2048}} (Meiji 40), it was designated as a Shinto shrine. Also, on November 1st of the same year, five nearby shrines were enshrined together: Kusatsu Otoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine), Abiko Shrine, Nunotahime Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine), Yamauchi Shrine, and Doso Shrine.

On October 1st, {{ill|1931|Q18782|qid=Q18782}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ka|შოვას პერიოდი|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}}6), the company status was promoted to {{ill|Fu-sha|qid=Q134917326}} {{Sfn|Oyora Shrine 4th seat (shikinaisha)|1977}}.

{{ill|1969|Q2485|qid=Q2485}} On September 29, 1969, the shrine building built in Manji 2 was destroyed by fire, so {{ill|1971|Q2475|qid=Q2475}} The shrine building was rebuilt with {{ill|reinforced concrete construction|Q1577013|qid=Q1577013}} on October 3, 1977.

== Precincts ==
* Main shrine - The current shrine building was built in {{ill|1971|Q2475|qid=Q2475}} (Showa 44) after being destroyed by a fire on September 29, 1969|Q2485}} (Showa 44). Reconstruction of {{ill|reinforced concrete construction|Q1577013|qid=Q1577013}} on October 3, 2007 {{Sfn|Oyora Shrine 4th seat (shikinaisha)|1977}}. Before it was destroyed by fire, it was built in {{ill|Manji (era)|Q1145295|qid=Q1145295}}2 ({{ill|1659|Q6995|qid=Q6995}}) and consisted of the main shrine, the shrine, and the worship hall. It was built |Q210684}} with a {{ill|Karahafu|Q977293|qid=Q977293}}, and the roof was {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}}. The old shrine building had a south-facing side near the north of the precincts, but during the reconstruction, it was changed to an east-facing side near the west side of the precincts.
* Seiden
* Hall of worship
* Shrine office
* Funeral hall
* South gate* Ryūjii (Ryuujii) - In the southwest corner of the precincts, there is a well called ``Ryuujini'' (Ryuujini), and there used to be a well called ``Niwa'' on the north side of the precincts {{Sfn|Oyira Shrine 4-za (Shikinai Shrine)|1977}}. It is said that a dragon snake living in {{ill|Yorami Pond|Q65248853|qid=Q65248853}} asked a farmer to remove the iron that had sunk in the pond, and in return, he promised rain if he offered water from the well and prayed. There is a legend that in the past, prayers for rain were actually held during times of drought. On the other hand, the garden can also be seen in the "Settsu Meisho Zue", and the place name of the enshrined area of ​​Oyora Shrine is also derived from this, but it is now buried and only a monument remains.

== About Goshu Shrine ==
Oyora Shrine was founded on November 1st, {{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}} (Meiji 40). Five shrines are enshrined together: Nunotahime Shrine (formerly {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mukakusha}}), Yamauchi Shrine (formerly Murasha), and Doso Shrine (formerly Mukakusha). The next two shrines, Kusatsu Otoshi Shrine and Nunotahime Shrine, will become Shikinai Shrines {{Sfn|Oyora Shrine 4-za (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1977}}.

; Kusatsu Otoshi Shrine
: ``Kusatsuooshijinja''. It was originally enshrined in Kanda, Niwa Village, Oaza Karita.
: ``Kusatsu Otoshi Shrine Kuwasizuku'' in Sumiyoshi District, Settsu Province in the ``Engishiki'' divine name book, and ``Nakatomi Sumuji no Kami'' in the annotation of the Sumiyoshi deity {{ill|Mikogami|Q352176|qid=Q352176}} of the Sumiyoshi deity {{ill|Mikogami|Q352176|qid=Q352176}} in the ``Sumiyoshi Taisha Jindaiki''. {{Sfn|Kusatsu Otoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1977}} (Akaru Hime no Mikoto Shrine, Shikinai Shrine Research Report Vol. 5, edited by Shikinai Shrine Research Group, Shikinai Shrine Research Group, 1977.</ref>). The entry ``Kuwazuku'' in the Shinmeicho means that the imperial court dedicated a hoe and a sewage bolt during the annual prayer festival. During the Meiji period, it was listed as a former village shrine, but was later enshrined with Oyora Shrine.: However, regarding ``Kusatsu Otoshi Shrine'' in the Shinmeicho, there is a theory that it is Otoshi Shrine, which is the outer branch shrine of Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine, as another Hideron shrine (the ``Shikiuchi Shrine Investigation Report'' considers the former Kusatsu Otoshi Shrine in Karita to be more likely) {{Sfn|Kusatsu Otoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1977}}.
; Nunotahime Shrine
: "Nunotahimejinja". It is said that it was originally enshrined in Sugimoto VillageAza Nukunota, but its location is currently unknown.
: It is compared to ``Tsunotahime no Mikoto Shrine'' in Sumiyoshi District, Settsu Province in the ``Engishiki'' divine name book, and to ``Nunotahime no Kami'' of the Sumiyoshi no Mikogami in ``Sumiyoshi Taisha Jindaiki.'' There is a theory that the god's name means the god of ``Nono-no-ta'' (rice fields) {{Sfn|Tsunotahime no Mikoto Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1977}}. During the Meiji period, it remained as a small shrine, and in 1872, it was listed as a former Mukakusha, but later it was enshrined with Oyora Shrine.
